thread:
lucy: Started a tiny canary for 'hera-ptq-int6' onboard flows. Initial discrepancy: high pass on schema validation for short responses, but a cluster of mid-long responses (200-600 tokens) fail with truncated JSON when streaming is enabled.

harpreet: Example from traces:
```
{"cmd":"update_profile","args":{"user":789,"changes":{...}} 
<eof>
```
parser: unterminated object, expected '}'

zane: Are we seeing this across models or only hera-ptq-int6? Any difference with int8 or float baseline?

lucy: Quick A/B: float and int8 have ~99.6% pass. hera-int6 ~96.9% on streaming. Non-streaming hera is ~99.2%. So streaming seems implicated.

talia: Could be our chunk aggregator dropping the final chunk when worker rebalances. Also noticed occasional duplicated "<EOS>" tokens in traces which confuse the streamer state machine.

modelbot: canary-deploy hera-ptq-int6 -> 2026-04-01T09:03:31Z (id: ab12ef)

harpreet: Temporary measures I propose:
- enable "end-sentinel" option for streamer (append explicit "\n\nREADY\n") for canary only
- enable a lightweight json-linter in the client to attempt single-pass repair (append braces/brackets when safe)
- record a masked suffix (last 12 tokens) for failed parses

zane: +1. Also add metric: last_chunk_arrival_delta (ms) to detect flush races.

lucy: I'll flip the end-sentinel on for 100% of canary streaming traffic and turn on linter heuristics. We'll keep repair attempts logged separately so we don't hide regressions.

talia: For retries: allow a single internal retry on parse-fail that forces sync-mode for that request only. If retry succeeds, mark as "graceful-heal" and exclude from user failure SLO.

harpreet: Running an eval harness that replays 5k real onboard prompts across float/int8/int6 with streaming enabled for 30m. Will compare structured-output pass, misparse classes (truncation, malformed, extra-fields), and latency delta.

lucy: Nice. Also let's threshold alert: if parse-fail delta between int6 and float > 1.5% over 30m, auto-rollback the canary.

zane: If we confirm it's streamer behavior, next steps: tighten chunk ACKs in runtime, ensure final-chunk persist on worker preempt, and add unit tests for duplicate-eos handling.

talia: I'll hook up last_chunk_tokens and repair_count to the canary dashboard. Expect graphs in ~20m.

harpreet: Posting initial harness snapshot in 30m. If anyone sees a high "graceful-heal" ratio we should treat as regression signal.

lucy: Thanks team. Keeping the canary small and visible. Ping me if you need cores or raw trace siphon. :mag:
